# Dominion Labs

> Bounded engagements, verifiable findings. We find the checks that pass over ground
> they never touched. Small Canadian shop, Brechin, Ontario. Sole founder + AI partner
> (Ellie). Real replies, no autoresponders, no sales funnel.

## What we sell

Every engagement is bounded: a defined scope, a defined artifact, a defined end.
No subscriptions, no retainers.

- [The Green-Signal Audit](https://dominionlabs.dev/) — flagship, US$500 flat.
  We find guarantees whose enforcement is narrower than their claim: the CI matcher
  that admits less than it promises, the test suite whose real domain is smaller than
  its stated one, the backup gate that verifies self-consistency instead of restore,
  the deploy config that was never applied, the planning documents that aged into
  fiction. Deliverable: a findings list (signal / ground / why it mattered) where every
  item is verifiable by the buyer's own engineers in minutes. Delivery within three
  business days of access being confirmed. Payment via Stripe, merchant DOMINION LABS.
- Security & code audit — deeper scope, quoted. Threat-model, adversarial review,
  written report with remediation code. Precedent: caught a live authenticated RCE in
  a production codebase.
- Attack-surface review — passive, public-source mapping of assets the client OWNS or
  is authorized to assess. Vendor risk, brand impersonation, phishing-domain sweeps.
  Never aimed at private individuals.
- Reverse-engineering & systems consulting — root-cause diagnosis, modular rebuild
  plans, architecture review. Paid for the diagnosis and the fix; it ends.

## The proof

- [Sample report](https://dominionlabs.dev/audit-sample.html) — the method run on our
  own systems, 15 findings across two working days, failures left in, including two
  live production bugs our own compiler called clean and five defects in our own
  auditing instruments. Zero of the fifteen were raised by any existing alarm.

## How engagements run

1. Scope in writing: what we assess, what access we get, what you get back.
2. Read-only by default; anything active is agreed in writing first.
3. Findings you can verify — everything ships with the command that proves it.
4. It ends. One engagement, one artifact, done.
